hints: Focus on bond angle, you are looking for any three atoms joined with a bond angle of 180 degrees.
Recall the shape around each carbon in poly(ethene) and propane, and around silicon in SiCl4, all are tetrahedral with angles of about 109.5 degrees.
Picture the octahedral shape of SF6 and notice what happens with the central S and any two opposite F atoms.
walkthrough:
**Understand what straight line means**

Three atoms in a straight line means the middle atom has two bonds pointing in exactly opposite directions. That is a bond angle of 180 degrees.

$$\text{straight line} = \text{bond angle of } 180^{\circ}$$

**Check the carbon compounds and SiCl4**

In poly(ethene), propane and $\text{SiCl}_4$, every central atom is tetrahedral. Each carbon is surrounded by 4 sigma bonds and $\text{Si}$ in $\text{SiCl}_4$ is also surrounded by 4 sigma bonds with no lone pairs.

$$\text{tetrahedral angle} \approx 109.5^{\circ} \text{, so no } 180^{\circ} \text{ line}$$

**Check the shape of sulfur hexafluoride**

In $\text{SF}_6$, sulfur has 6 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so the shape is octahedral with 90 degree angles between neighbours. But any two F atoms opposite each other across the S give $\text{F-S-F}$ in a perfect straight line.

$$90^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \text{ for trans F-S-F}$$

**Make the conclusion**

Only the octahedral molecule contains a linear three-atom unit. That is sulfur hexafluoride, where opposite fluorines are collinear with sulfur.

options.A: Incorrect. In poly(ethene), $\text{-(CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{)-}_n$, each carbon is tetrahedral with about 109.5 degrees between bonds. The chain is zig-zag, not straight, so no three bonded atoms are collinear.
options.B: Incorrect. In propane, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$, each carbon is tetrahedral. The C-C-C angle is about 109.5 degrees, so the three carbons form a bent shape, not a straight line.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{SiCl}_4$ is tetrahedral with Cl-Si-Cl angles of 109.5 degrees. Students sometimes think four identical bonds might include a straight line, but tetrahedral geometry has no 180 degree angle.
options.D: Correct. $\text{SF}_6$ is octahedral. Adjacent F-S-F angles are 90 degrees, but opposite (trans) F atoms lie at 180 degrees to each other through S, so F-S-F is a straight line of three atoms.
